47014.subject: English Language
47014.question_text: According to this passage, it gives the child great pleasure
47014.explanation: According to the passage, the child ''enjoys causing the same tower to waver and collapse''. He enjoys destroying the tower himself.

options.text: for Daddy to see the tower he has built
to see his tower accidentally destroyed
to be helped to destroy the tower

47015.subject: English Language
47015.question_text: What other feeling does the child derive from the fall of his tower apart from pleasure?

47016.subject: English Language
47016.question_text: How does the author try to explain this ‘destructive stage'?
47016.explanation: The author explains the destructive stage by creating a supposition of a child's destructive personality born out of the experience of sudden falls at the very time when standing upright on wobbly legs

options.text: It is the last stage in child development
The child wants to displease his parents
It grows out of the child's recent experiences of sudden falls
The child is just going through a destructive stage

47017.subject: English Language
47017.question_text: The expression 'must kick it and make it collapse' in this context means
47017.explanation: The child's inability to follow his mother's advice reveals an irresistible urge to demolish

options.text: is forced to kick it and demolish it
is obliged to kick it and make it collapse
cannot resist the urge to demolish it
ought to kick it and make it collapse

47019.subject: English Language
47019.question_text: From the way the story ended, it can be concluded that the

options.text: lamb did not survive the encounter
wolf and the lamb parted amicably
wolf had encountered the lamb's parents
lamb offended the wolf quite seriously

47020.subject: English Language
47020.question_text: The expression 'when this excuse failed him' suggests that the
47020.explanation: The passage provides the Wolf's thought of wanting to find a pretext(reason) to devour the lamb. This justifies option A as the correct answer.

options.text: wolf only made up the charges levelled against the lamb
lamb was more intelligent than the wolf
lamb was prepared for the charges levelled against him
wolf was uncertain of the charges levelled against the lamb

47021.subject: English Language
47021.question_text: The charges levelled against the lamb are

47022.subject: English Language
47022.question_text: The expression angry tone and terrible aspect refers to the wolf’s
47022.explanation:
The phrase "angry tone and terrible aspect" describes two things:

  • Angry tone → the way the wolf speaks, suggesting a harsh voice.
  • Terrible aspect → the wolf's appearance or manner, suggesting a menacing (threatening) posture or look.

Therefore, "harsh voice and menacing posture" best captures the meaning of the expression.

47023.subject: English Language
47023.question_text: Which of the following aptly describes the moral of the story?

options.text: the sins of the forefathers are visited upon the children no matter how long it takes
if you have made up your mind to hang your dog, any rope will do for the purpose
the law is weak in defence of the poor against the rich and mighty
no matter how highly placed he is in society, the unmindful lawbreaker will always meet his nemesis.

47024.subject: English Language
47024.question_text: Choose the option that best completes the gap, I'll find time for my _________ when I get _________with this difficult assignment.
47024.explanation: Pastime implies an activity that someone does regularly for enjoyment rather than work , while get through implies to pass a difficult experience

47025.subject: English Language
47025.explanation: Paid off means to become worthwhile or to produce a benefit.

47027.subject: English Language
47027.question_text: Choose the option that best completes the gap. The chairman refused to shake __________ with the secretary
47027.explanation: When you shake hands with someone you take their right hand in your own for a few moments, often moving it up and down slightly

47028.subject: English Language
47028.question_text: Choose the option that best completes the gap. Wherever the leader went people struggled to catch a __________ of him
47028.explanation: To catch a glimpse of someone or something means to briefly look at someone or to briefly see the person or thing. The verb ‘catch’ cannot be used with ‘look’ in option B, ‘view’ in option C and ‘picture’ in option D.

47029.subject: English Language
47029.question_text: Choose the option that best completes the gap. Mrs. Okoro __________ in this school since 1975
47029.explanation: 'Since' implies from a specified time in the past. A present perfect progressive tense describes an event in a progressive form that started in the past and ended in the present. 'has been teaching' is an example of a verb element associated with a present perfect progressive tense

47030.subject: English Language
47030.question_text: Choose the option that best completes the gap.  I was seriously disappointed when the __________ between the two teams ended in a goalless draw
47030.explanation: A match means a competitive sport event between two teams

47031.subject: English Language
47031.question_text: Choose the option that best completes the gap. The young man looked carefully at the long document, but he couldn't make __________ what it meant
47031.explanation: To make out;  means to understand something. Simply put, he couldn't understand what it meant.

47033.subject: English Language
47033.question_text: Choose the option that best completes the gap. While the worshippers closed their eyes in prayer, a thief made __________ with the collection
47033.explanation: Made away means to steal or abduct

47034.subject: English Language
47034.question_text:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.

If you keep playing with this door handle, it will get __________
47034.explanation: The sentence refers to the door handle becoming "loose", which means not tightly fixed or secure. This is the correct word to describe the state of the handle. "Loose" here is used as an adjective to describe the state of the door handle if it continues to be played with.

47041.subject: English Language
47041.question_text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined. For all he cared: the game was as good as lost
47041.explanation: The expression “for all he cared” means that someone is completely unconcerned or indifferent about something. So the sentence: For all he cared, the game was as good as lost means he did not care at all whether the game was lost or not.

options.text: He did not care if the game as lost
He could not care less if the game was lost
He was almost certain that the game would be lost
He was afraid the game would be lost

47042.subject: English Language
47042.question_text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined. The meeting was cancelled because of the convocation
47042.explanation:
To cancel implies to decide/ announce that an event will not take place.

Call off means to decide that something will not happen

47043.subject: English Language
47043.question_text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined. Ayodeji is an ardent supporter of education for the child

47044.subject: English Language
47044.question_text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined. The exhibition was an eye opener to all
47044.explanation: Exhibition means a public display of woks of art or items of interest

47045.subject: English Language
47045.question_text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined. As a Journalist, Bola has always had a nose for stories
47045.explanation: To have a nose for something means to have an instinct or a natural ability to find/ recognize something

47046.subject: English Language
47046.question_text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined. Nwankwo was on the verge of signing a two-year contract with the club
47046.explanation:
To be on the verge of something means to be very close to it.

To be on the brink also means to be on the edge or border of something.

47047.subject: English Language
47047.question_text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined. The Governor told the chief that he was only on a routine tour
47047.explanation: Routine means performed as part of a regular procedure

47048.subject: English Language
47048.question_text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined. The new ruler is big-hearted in his dealing with the people

47049.subject: English Language
47049.question_text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined. The essay topic is nebulous

47050.subject: English Language
47050.question_text: Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence. The events of last Friday show that there is no love lost between the Principal and the Vice-principal
47050.explanation: The term no love lost signifies ill will exclusively. If there is no love lost between two people, they have a strong enmity towards or hate for the other and make no effort to conceal it.

47051.subject: English Language
47051.question_text: Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence. If he were here, it could be more fun
47051.explanation:
The first clause 'if he were here' reveals an unreal conditional statement that signifies the absence of someone. However the second clause 'it could be more fun'  signifies the presence of little fun.

Option A is the best answer

options.text: He did not show up and so the occasion lacked much fun
He was being expected to supply more fun
There was no fun because he was not present
He was expected but did not show up to liven up the occasion

47052.subject: English Language
47052.question_text: Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence. Adawo is an Imp
47052.explanation:
An imp is a person with mischievous behaviour.

Option D is the correct answer.

47053.subject: English Language
47053.question_text:
Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

The man reasoned that there ought to be a limit to sycophancy
47053.explanation:
sycophancy;  using of flattery compliments to gain self-serving favour or advantage from another person.

Option C is correct. 
''The man reasoned that there ought to be a limit to sycophancy'' means that, they should be a limit to how people use flattery compliments on people especially when they stand to gain something in return.

options.text: there can be no favour beyond a reasonable point
sycophants need not talk all the time
people should know when not to use flattery
sycophants should know when to grant people requests

47054.subject: English Language
47054.question_text: Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence. The organization is constantly in a state of flux
47054.explanation: A state of flux means a state of uncertainty about what should be done usually followed by the establishment of a new direction of action, Flux is used to describe something that constantly changes

options.text: There are periodic changes in the organization
The organization is facing a difficult period
The organization is experiencing; good times

47055.subject: English Language
47055.question_text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) or phrase in italics.

The witness averred that she had seen Dosun at the scene of the crime
47055.explanation:
To aver means to establish a fact or assert a truth.

To deny means to disprove of a statement. It is the opposite of ‘aver’.

47056.subject: English Language
47056.question_text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) or phrase in italics.

The governor's visit is an unprecedented event in the history of the social club
47056.explanation:
unprecedented; means something that has never done or known before.
Something that is remarkable.

Option C ''Insignificant'' is the correct option. It means simply means something that is meaningless; too small or unimportant to be worth consideration.

47057.subject: English Language
47057.question_text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) or phrase in italics. Our principal took exception to the ignoble role the teacher played in the matter
47057.explanation: ignoble implies not honourable in character or purpose

47058.subject: English Language
47058.question_text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) or phrase in italics. He is notorious for his drunkenness
47058.explanation:
Notorious means famous or well known for some bad qualities.

Renowned means famous for something for good qualities

47059.subject: English Language
47059.question_text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) or phrase in italics.

The severity of the harmattan helped me to complete my writing assignment in record time because i had no choice but to lock myself indoors
47059.explanation: severity is the state of being severe . the degree of something being bad or undesirable very great; intense. while the opposite of severity is mildness which means not severe; gentle.

47060.subject: English Language
47060.question_text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) or phrase in italics. This card entitles you to attend the film show
47060.explanation:
‘Entitle’ means to qualify, allow or give someone the right to do something

‘Disqualify’ means to make one ineligible to do something.

47061.subject: English Language
47061.question_text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) or phrase in italics. He is loved for his altruism
47061.explanation:
Altruism means to have regard for others at the expense of oneself.

Selfishness means to always consider one’s own interest before others.

47062.subject: English Language
47062.question_text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) or phrase in italics. The Journalist said he was working freelance
47062.explanation:
To work freelance means to work randomly without having a long-term contract with any firm or person.

Dependent means to rely on a particular person or thing. It is the antonym of ‘freelance’ in this context.

47063.subject: English Language
47063.question_text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) or phrase in italics. The Flying Eagles put up a plucky defence against their opponents
47063.explanation:
Plucky means showing courage in difficult situations.

Weak means lacking energy or force.

47064.subject: English Language
47064.question_text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) or phrase in italics. We found a shady place for the display
47064.explanation: Shady means situated in or full of shade

47065.subject: English Language
47065.question_text: Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap. The sea wave continue to ____________ the cliff on the west coast constantly
47065.explanation: Erode means to gradually wear away or gradually disappear. Erode is used in a context that relates to wind, water or other natural agents.

47066.subject: English Language
47066.question_text: Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap. I would have been surprised if you ____________ the orange
47066.explanation: 'Would have' is used in conditional statements to talk about something that did not happen in the past. In the sequence of tenses, if the main clause contains 'would have', the conditional subordinate clause should be in its past participle.

47067.subject: English Language
47067.question_text: Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap. By the time the plane reaches Harare, it __________in the air for twelve hours
47067.explanation: 'By the time' is an adverb of time that can be used in the present, past and future tense. The question is, however, in the present tense which will be needing a present perfect tense to complete the sentence.

47068.subject: English Language
47068.question_text: Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap. The patient is suffering from ____________
47068.explanation: The options contain miss spellings of the word, RHEUMATISM.

47069.subject: English Language
47069.question_text: Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap. We saw Ifueko ____________ an egg on the wall
47069.explanation:
‘Smash’ is the correct answer because the action conveyed is a single action.

In reported statements, writers/ speakers should retain the present tense.

47070.subject: English Language
47070.question_text:
Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap.

Knowledge of figures of speech as well as of idiom and lexical items ____________ in this section
47070.explanation:
When either of these words is used; as well as, together with, alongside, no less than e.t.c, the subject of the clause would be the noun or pronoun that comes before the marker of accompaniment. 

Knowledge of figures of speech is a singular subject that should agree with a singular verb

47071.subject: English Language
47071.question_text: Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap. The answers to the questions were discussed ____________ the students
47071.explanation: 'By' is the best answer to this question. Between can not be considered because the question did not explicitly tell us the number of students involved.

47072.subject: English Language
47072.question_text:
Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap.

The shipping company advertised for ____________ accountants
47072.explanation: The shipping company advertised for two young, but highly competent Nigerian accountants

options.text: two young but highly competent Nigerian
young but highly competent two Nigerian
two Nigerian, young, but highly competent
highly competent, but young, two Nigerian

47073.subject: English Language
47073.question_text: Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap. If it had rained, we would have had to postpone the concert. It didn't rain, so ____________
47073.explanation: The conditional statement ended with the first sentence. The following statement should therefore end with a past tense

47074.subject: English Language
47074.question_text: Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap. Now, I am used ____________ bread without butter
47074.explanation:
eating is present participle. 

used is an adjective that qualiffied the verb eating. therefore it is is right to say ''to eating'' rightly fits into that statement

I am used to eating bread without butter.

47075.subject: English Language
47075.question_text: Choose the option that has a different stress pattern from the others.
47075.explanation:
1. ability has its stress pattern on the second syllable

2. registration has its stress pattern on the third syllable

3. quadruplicate has its stress pattern on the second syllable

4. revivalist has its stress pattern on the second syllable

 

Registration, therefore, has a different stress pattern from the rest with its stress on the 2nd syllable

47076.subject: English Language
47076.question_text: Choose the option that has a different stress pattern from the others.
47076.explanation: All the words are stressed on the first syllable except 'represent' which is stressed on the last syllable.

47077.subject: English Language
47077.question_text:
Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letter(s) underlined.

thatch
47077.explanation: 'Method' has the same consonant sound as the letters underlined in the word 'thatch'

47078.subject: English Language
47078.question_text:
Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letter(s) underlined.

chateau

47079.subject: English Language
47079.question_text:
Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letter(s) emboldened.

Joint

47452.subject: English Language
47452.question_text: choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) in italics. The manager commended the players for the narrow victory.
47452.explanation: Narrow here means close or small margin.

47456.subject: English Language
47456.question_text:
choose the option that best completes the gap(s).

  I am not sure that all _____ well with John.
47456.explanation:
All is well is when it refers to everything.

The question, all is well is most appropriate because the context is used to refer to everything and not everyone in a group

47463.subject: English Language
47463.question_text: choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined. Thousands of students are candidates for the examination but only very few pass
47463.explanation: Enter for implies to partake, participate or take part in something

47529.subject: English Language
47529.question_text: choose the option that best completes the gap(s). We look forward to _______ from you very soon.
47529.explanation: The expression ‘look forward to’ must be followed with a gerund.

47531.subject: English Language
47531.question_text:
choose the option nearest in meaning to the italicized words or expressions.

  The French classes were always funny because we considered French a strange tongue.
47531.explanation:
Strange means unfamiliar.

Foreign means originating from another country.

47532.subject: English Language
47532.question_text:
choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) in italics.

  Everyone testifies to the unique taste of our flavor.
47532.explanation: The word “unique” means one of a kind, rare or unlike anything else. Common is correct because it means ordinary, widespread or not special.

47536.subject: English Language
47536.question_text: Choose the option that best completes the gap. All God's prophets were given the great __________ to preach salvation to people
47536.explanation:
Commission means a task or mission to accomplish.

Take note of the double ‘s’ and the double ‘m’. All other options are wrongly spelt

47538.subject: English Language
47538.question_text:
choose the option that best completes the gap(s).

The principal _________ our mobile phones.
47538.explanation:
Note the correct spelling of ‘seize’.

To seize a thing means to deliberately take hold of it for a period of time

47539.subject: English Language
47539.question_text:
choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap(s).

For fear of being caught, the thief shouted and cursed the slow bank manager in a language ________much for words.
47539.explanation:
"For fear of being caught, the thief shouted and cursed the slow bank manager in a language too much for words." 

The phrase “too much for words” is an idiomatic expression used to describe something so intense or extreme that it's difficult or impossible to describe. In this context, the thief’s language (probably abusive or vulgar) was too extreme to be expressed properly in words.

47540.subject: English Language
47540.question_text:
choose the option nearest in meaning to the italicized words or expressions.

  The coach invited me to his office having found me mettlesome
47540.explanation: Mettlesome means to be courageous. The correct answer is A

47541.subject: English Language
47541.question_text:
choose the option that best completes the gap(s).

You may now ___________ with your presentation.

47542.subject: English Language
47542.question_text:
choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) in italics.

  Father Francis thanked God for the abundance of blessings his family received
47542.explanation:
Abundance means an excessive availability of something.

Paucity means fewness in number

47544.subject: English Language
47544.question_text:
choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap(s).

  The pastor asked the women to _________ their hearts to God in prayers.
47544.explanation:
To bare one’s mind means to reveal or uncover all that is in it.

  Note the spelling.

47545.subject: English Language
47545.question_text:
choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap(s).

  We saw you earlier but we could not stop you because we did not know __________.
47545.explanation: The expression is in its past tense and should maintain a past tense all through

47546.subject: English Language
47546.question_text:
choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) in italics.

  It is customary to find young men and women in sports.
47546.explanation:
Customary means habitual or conventional.

Unusual means unlike what is expected.It is the antonym of ‘customary’

47547.subject: English Language
47547.question_text:
choose the option nearest in meaning to the italicized words or expressions.

  High mortality rate is becoming increasingly predominant.
47547.explanation:
‘Predominant’ means common, significant and important.

‘Rampant’ means common and unrestrained.

47548.subject: English Language
47548.question_text:
choose the option nearest in meaning to the italicized words or expressions.

  The rapist claimed that the woman’s voluptuous hips attracted him

47549.subject: English Language
47549.question_text:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

  Grandma told the boys a story that cheered them up.
47549.explanation:
To cheer one up means to make them happy especially after having been sad.

To be delighted means to be happy. The correct answer is C.

47550.subject: English Language
47550.question_text:
choose the option that best completes the gap.

  The cliff is popularly known for ___________ morning beauty.

47551.subject: English Language
47551.question_text:
select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

  The team adapted to the new tactic as clean as a whistle.
47551.explanation: The expression ‘as clean as a whistle’ means perfectly and without errors.

options.text: They adapted to the pattern perfectly
They needed a whistle to be able to adapt to the pattern.
They adapted to the tactic with little errors
They found it difficult to adapt to the new tactic.

47553.subject: English Language
47553.question_text:
choose the option opposite in meaning to the word(s) in italics.

  The driver was discharged while the car owner was ___________ for fraud.
47553.explanation:
To discharge someone means to legally release them from confinement.

To remand means to be charged and awaiting trials.

47554.subject: English Language
47554.question_text:
choose the option nearest in meaning to the italicized words or expressions.

  The police later discovered that Audu feigned death.
47554.explanation:
To feign means to make a false show of something.

To fake something means to make a false display.
